plants.name: Paeonia lactiflora
plants.description: A long-lived herbaceous perennial with large, fragrant, bowl-shaped to fully double flowers held above glossy, deeply divided foliage. It is a classic cottage garden and cut-flower favorite that thrives in regions with cold winters.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (May to June in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to China, Mongolia, and Siberia; widely cultivated in temperate gardens across North America, Europe, and Asia
plants.funFact: Peonies can live and bloom for over 50 years in the same spot, and in China they have been cultivated for more than 1,500 years as symbols of prosperity and honor.

plants.name: Iris germanica
plants.description: A rhizomatous perennial with sword-shaped gray-green leaves and showy flowers with three upright standards, three drooping falls, and a fuzzy 'beard' on each fall. Hybrids come in nearly every color combination imaginable.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring (May to early June in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Origins in the Mediterranean region; cultivated throughout temperate gardens in Europe, North America, and Australia
plants.funFact: The iris is named after the Greek goddess of the rainbow, Iris, and the dried rhizomes (orris root) are used as a fixative in perfumes.

plants.name: Rosa canina
plants.description: A vigorous, arching, thorny deciduous shrub that produces delicate, lightly scented five-petaled flowers, followed by bright red rose hips in autumn. It scrambles through hedgerows and woodland edges.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (May to July)
plants.location: Native to Europe, northwest Africa, and western Asia; commonly seen in British and European hedgerows
plants.funFact: During World War II, Britons collected rose hips from dog roses to make vitamin C-rich syrup, since citrus imports were scarce.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A medium to large tree with fern-like foliage that erupts in clouds of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers. In the Northern Hemisphere tropics and subtropics it blooms in late spring, carpeting streets with fallen petals.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer in the Northern Hemisphere (May to June); spring in the Southern Hemisphere (October to November)
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in Mexico, Southern California, Florida, Hawaii, India, and parts of Africa
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, jacarandas are so abundant that the city is nicknamed the 'Jacaranda City', and some cultures believe a falling blossom on your head brings good luck.
